result.finding: Assessed 5 CWE rules in Credentials & Secrets: 1 FOUND, 4 NOT_FOUND
evidence: Full-repository source assessment, not a changed-code review. Reviewed all application Java, JavaScript, templates, runtime/deployment configuration and Oracle initialization scripts. Tests reviewed as corroboration, not counted as production vulnerabilities. Excluded generated target output, assessment outputs, skill instructions and .github/agents.

Static assessment only; no deployed application, native dependency internals, runtime exploitation or stress testing. NOT_FOUND denotes no confirmed application-source match, not a guarantee of security.

CWE-259: Runtime database and admin passwords are required external environment/property values with no built-in password fallback. Oracle scripts require ORACLE_PWD and APP_USER_PASSWORD. .env.example contains explicit replace-me examples, not active production credentials. Test-only empty H2 password is not a production finding. Credential literals intentionally omitted; references retained.

CWE-321: No hard-coded encryption/signing key or KeySpec initialization in application source/configuration. BCryptPasswordEncoder generates salts; random photo UUIDs are identifiers, not cryptographic keys.

CWE-732: Oracle grants are schema-scoped CREATE privileges and quota, not DBA or system-wide ANY access. Upload/delete require authentication; gallery reads are intentionally public. No world-writable critical file mode, exposed management privilege or confirmed permission assignment enabling an unintended actor was found. Root default container user and publicly bound ports are hardening concerns, not alone a demonstrated CWE-732 instance.

CWE-778: Security-critical upload and irreversible delete operations record only filenames/photo IDs, never the authenticated actor, request correlation or caller identity. DetailController.deletePhoto and PhotoServiceImpl log successful deletion without Principal/SecurityContext information. No application audit listener/repository or audit trail captures this omitted attribution. Thus the logs cannot establish which authenticated caller performed a destructive action. Normal operation/error logs exist; this finding is missing important security-event detail, not a claim that the application has no logging. Current configuration defines one shared admin account, further limiting individual attribution.

CWE-798: Default admin/database usernames are public identifiers, not a complete embedded credential. Authentication passwords are externally supplied and required; no fixed token, cryptographic key or executable default password found. Example placeholders are documented as non-reusable; no credential literal copied into assessment.

values.name: Use of Hard-coded Password
values.description: The product contains a hard-coded password, which it uses for its own inbound authentication or for outbound communication to external components.

values.name: Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key
values.description: The product uses a hard-coded, unchangeable cryptographic key.

values.name: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource
values.description: The product specifies permissions for a security-critical resource in a way that allows that resource to be read or modified by unintended actors.

values.name: Insufficient Logging
values.description: When a security-critical event occurs, the product either does not record the event or omits important details about the event when logging it.
